facts: The word ballet comes from the Italian word ballare, which means to dance.
Ballet steps have French names because ballet grew up at the royal court of France.
King Louis XIV of France loved to dance. He started the first dance academy in 1661.
Pointe shoes are made from layers of fabric, paper and glue. There is no wood inside!
Plié means bent in French. Every ballet class starts with them.
Relevé means raised in French. That's you going up onto the balls of your feet.
Jeté means thrown in French, because you throw your leg into the jump.
Chassé means chased in French. One foot chases the other!
Port de bras means carriage of the arms. Your arms dance too!
Dancers spot, keeping their eyes on one point, so they don't get dizzy when they turn.
The arabesque is named after swirly patterns in Arabic art.
The Nutcracker ballet was first performed in 1892 in St. Petersburg, Russia.
Tchaikovsky wrote the music for The Nutcracker, Swan Lake and Sleeping Beauty.
Jazz dance grew up alongside jazz music in the United States in the early 1900s.
Hip hop dance started in New York City in the 1970s.
Tap dance has roots in African American dance mixed with Irish and English step dancing.
Martha Graham was a famous modern dance pioneer. She invented the idea of contraction and release.
Contemporary dance mixes ideas from ballet, jazz and modern dance.
Dancing makes your heart pump faster, so it's a workout for your heart.
Warming up before you stretch makes your muscles stretchier and safer.
Sleep helps your brain remember new choreography. Bedtime is practice too!
Pirouette is French for spinning around, like a top.
challenges: Balance in passé for 10 seconds. Eyes up!

Teach someone at home one move from your dance.

Do 10 relevés while you brush your teeth.
Run your solo once with your best performance smile the whole time.
Say all the counts of your solo out loud.
Make up a brand new 4-count move and give it a name.
Point your feet for one whole TV show.
Do your best jazz hands for 8 counts. Sparkle!
Practice your show bow three times.
Show your dance pet your favorite move.
Warm up, then stretch your splits for 30 seconds on each side.
Do your trio part and imagine Hannah and Lauren next to you.
Spot a point on the wall and do 3 slow turns.
